scenario: AITA for not staying home and taking care of my sick wife all weekend? | On Thursday evening my wife started feeling unwell. I encouraged her to go to bed and told her I could handle the kids evening stuff by myself (3 kids, ages 9, 11, and 13). I checked on her after the kids were in bed at 9 and she was fevered- I asked if she wanted any medicine, made sure she had some water, and rubbed her back for a few minutes. I slept in the spare room but got up twice to check on her. The next morning I got the kids ready and off to school, went to a meeting and came home at 10 to take her to the doctor. I worked from home until our cleaning lady came around 1 and asked her to keep an eye on my wife and went back into the office for a couple meetings, picked up the kids and was home around 4. Her fever broke shortly after I got home at 4 and I helped her shower. Our oldest had a school dance and I got some movies and set the youngest 2 up in the den for the evening with pizza and some games so they'd be quiet. I checked on my wife periodically and after the oldest got home me and the 3 kids camped out in the den. On Saturday morning, the kids were restless so I took them out for the day bc I didn't want them to be around the house being loud. I checked on my wife and she was sleeping- I refilled her water and left her a note. Throughout the day I called and sent her messages and my mom took her over some homemade soup and checked on her. We were gone the majority of the day but the kids came home worn out and we crashed in the den again. I checked on my wife as soon as we got home and she was looking better. Sunday morning, the kids and I woke up early, did some yardwork then went to the store to do the weekly grocery shopping. When we got home my wife was up and about and still weak but feeling better. However, she was being really short with me and was in a bad mood. I thought it was just bc she didn't feel well but after a few hours of her making snide comments I asked her if something was wrong and she exploded on me that her family abandoned her while she was sick. She went off about how she always takes care of us when we're sick but we avoided her like the plague and didn't stay home and I made the cleaning lady and my mom take care of her instead of doing it myself. I tried to explain that I didn't want to expose the kids to being sick and I didn't want them around the house being loud while she was trying to rest and I checked on her multiple times. She said I should've sent the kids to my parents or something and stayed home and she can't believe I didn't sleep with her for 3 days. I starting getting angry and told her that I did what I thought was best and she sounded ungrateful bc it wasn't exactly what she would've done. She then called me an asshole. We went to bed angry and didn't really speak this morning. I keep stewing over this bc I don't think that I'm an asshole but maybe I am?

Her fever broke shortly after I got home at 4, and I helped her shower. Our oldest had a school dance, so I got some movies and set the youngest two up in the den for the evening with pizza and some games so they'd be quiet. I checked on my wife periodically, and after the oldest got home, me and the three kids camped out in the den. On Saturday morning, the kids were restless, so I took them out for the day because I didn't want them to be around the house being loud. I checked on my wife, and she was sleeping. I refilled her water and left her a note. Throughout the day, I called and sent her messages, and my mom took her over some homemade soup and checked on her. We were gone the majority of the day, but the kids came home worn out, and we crashed in the den again. I checked on my wife as soon as we got home, and she was looking better. Sunday morning, the kids and I woke up early, did some yard work, then went to the store to do the weekly grocery shopping. When we got home, my wife was up and about and still weak but feeling better. However, she was being really short with me and was in a bad mood. I thought it was just because she didn't feel well, but after a few hours of her making snide comments, I asked her if something was wrong, and she exploded at me, saying her family abandoned her while she was sick. She went off about how she always takes care of us when we're sick but we avoided her like the plague and didn't stay home and made the cleaning lady and my mom take care of her instead of doing it myself. I tried to explain that I didn't want to expose the kids to being sick and I didn't want them around the house being loud while she was trying to rest, and I checked on her multiple times. Alright, so I need to figure out if I did the right thing or not. Let's break it down. First, when my wife was sick, I took care of the kids and made sure she had what she needed. I checked on her multiple times, got her to the doctor, and even helped her shower when her fever broke. I also made arrangements for the kids to have a quiet evening and took them out on Saturday to give her some peace. I involved my mom to help check on her, and I made sure she had soup and water. On the other hand, my wife felt abandoned because I didn't stay home with her and instead relied on the cleaning lady and my mom to help. She was upset that I didn't sleep with her for three days and that I didn't stay home to take care of her exclusively. So, is it right or wrong for me to not stay home and take care of my sick wife all weekend? Did I prioritize the kids' needs and my work over her well-being? Or was I just trying to manage everything as best as I could? I think it's important to consider both perspectives. On one side, I was handling the kids, ensuring they were taken care of, and making sure my wife had the necessary support. On the other side, my wife felt neglected because I wasn't physically present with her all the time. Maybe there's a balance that could have been struck. Perhaps I could have stayed home more, but also made arrangements for the kids to be with my parents or another trusted person so that I could be with my wife without the kids being around. That way, I could have provided the care she needed while still ensuring the kids were taken care of. I also need to think about communication. Did I explain my reasons clearly to my wife? It seems like I tried to, but maybe in the heat of the moment, it came off as defensive. Maybe if I had approached the conversation differently, she would have felt more understood. Another thing to consider is the cultural or personal expectations around caregiving. In some cultures, it's expected that the husband would stay home to care for the sick wife, while in others, it's more common for both partners to share responsibilities or seek external help. I also wonder about the long-term effects of this situation. If my wife feels consistently unsupported when she's sick, it could lead to resentment or a breakdown in our relationship. On the other hand, if I always put her needs above everything else, it could strain my ability to manage other responsibilities. Perhaps I should reflect on what I can do differently in the future to prevent similar conflicts. Maybe setting up a plan in advance for when one of us is sick, so that both our needs are addressed. Or having a conversation about our expectations regarding caregiving. In the end, I think it's a complex situation with no clear right or wrong answer. It depends on the specific circumstances, our relationship dynamics, and our individual needs and priorities. However, it's clear that communication and finding a balance are key to resolving such conflicts and ensuring both partners feel supported.
